Whole declaration fidelity is unclear on two independent grounds. Ratio semantics: C06 Statement literally says requires 1/6700 without an approximation qualifier, but E05 Expected outcome explicitly says expected ~1/6700 ratio, and Table 8 reports rounded scientific-notation operands 1.35e10 and 9.04e14. The source therefore does not unambiguously authorize exact equality rather than a rounded magnitude; the weaker 1%-cost falsifier does not authorize either an equality tolerance or replacing the 1/6700 claim with merely cheaper. The two declared ratio_ge/ratio_le properties at the identical target 6700 encode exact mathematical equality, not rounded-ratio equivalence. Inspection of _gate.py shows both have the same margin and positive printed-precision gate: at exact equality they are inconclusive, while outside the gate one inequality fails, so the conjunction cannot recognize equality as holding. This is semantic inspection, not an executed verdict. No source-defined ratio band or rounding tolerance is supplied, and the printed operands imply roughly 66963 rather than 6700; that numerical discrepancy is a source inconsistency, not a source-confirmed falsification of a tolerance the source never defines. Replay scope: the two-sided factor-two bound is grounded in within-2x, but properties 2-3 restrict EM Drop to FLAN-T5Large Full FT, whereas the statement only expressly scopes the FLOP example to that setting and its C04 dependency/Table 3 spans four replay settings; FLAN-T53B LoRA has 0.138 versus 0.030 (4.6-fold). Recommendation separately: conservatively leave the whole claim undeclared while clarifying exact-versus-rounded ratio semantics, any authorized tolerance, and replay-comparability scope; do not manufacture a band, repair the numerical claim, shrink the original denominator, or describe an unrun result as a source-confirmed violation.
